stem: In a village field in Punjab, Meena watches cattle egrets walking beside grazing buffaloes. The egrets eat insects that the buffaloes disturb, so the egrets get food easily, while the buffaloes are neither helped nor harmed. Which type of relationship is this?

options.text: mutualism, because both the egret and the buffalo benefit
commensalism, because the egret benefits and the buffalo is unaffected
parasitism, because the egret benefits and the buffalo is harmed
competition, because the egret and the buffalo share the same food

teacher.key_rationale: The egret gains food while the buffalo is neither helped nor harmed, which defines commensalism. Option A is the trap for students who assume any friendly association benefits both; C traps students who assume one organism gaining always means the other is harmed.
